profile.reading:
Sabey Data Centers operates SDC Seattle, a two-part data center campus in Tukwila, King County, Washington, marketed by the operator as the West Coast's largest privately owned data center campus. Sabey traces its roots to 1972, when Dave Sabey founded Sabey Corporation as a Pacific Northwest commercial real estate developer; the company entered the data center business almost by accident during the dot-com collapse, when a vacated tenant building in this same Tukwila location became SDC Seattle Building 5, prompting Sabey's pivot into the data center industry. Sabey Data Centers itself was formally established in 2010 as a joint venture between Sabey Corporation and institutional investor National Real Estate Advisors, a structure confirmed on both the operator's own site and independently by Wikipedia. As of 2026 Sabey operates seven data center campuses nationally, together totaling more than 3.5 million square feet and, per Wikipedia's most recent figure, nearly 400 MW of capacity; Tim Mirick became Sabey's president effective January 1, 2025, succeeding Rob Rockwood.

Per the operator's own SDC Seattle page, the Tukwila campus totals more than a million square feet and 54 MW of capacity campus-wide, a figure not broken out per individual building and not applied to any single structure here. Aggregator sourcing indicates the campus actually comprises two separately addressed sub-campuses: Intergate.East, at a street range of 3311 to 3511 South 120th Place, Tukwila, WA 98168, spanning roughly 1.2 million square feet; and Intergate.West, at 12101 to 12301 Tukwila International Boulevard, Tukwila, WA 98168, built in 1999 and spanning roughly 173,000 square feet.

This building, Intergate.West Building C, is listed by aggregator DatacenterHawk at 12101 Tukwila International Boulevard, Tukwila, WA 98168, matching the lower bound of the campus-wide range described by other aggregator sources, at the opposite end of the block from neighboring Building B (12201).
profile.capacity_note: not published at the building level. Campus wide total is 54 MW (operator figure) across the Tukwila campus, not applied to this individual building.
profile.research_note: Gap-view review: Sabey publishes SDC Seattle only as a campus-wide total (1M+ sqft / 54MW across Intergate.East + Intergate.West sub-campuses), not broken out per building. No per-building figure exists for Intergate.West Building C. No numeric key written.

reading.body:
Intergate Seattle West Building C is one of three structures on the Intergate.West sub-campus in Tukwila, occupying roughly 173,000 square feet across the two-building Western portion of SDC Seattle. The operator publishes 54 MW of capacity for the entire Tukwila campus but does not break this figure out by building, so the IT load and rack density of this specific structure are not public. Intergate.West was built in 1999 and sits at the lower end of a contiguous address range spanning 12101 to 12301 Tukwila International Boulevard.

Washington state has 46 mapped data center facilities, but only two publish capacity figures; SDC Seattle ranks third statewide at 54 MW campus-wide, representing 90 percent of the state's 60 MW of published capacity. This concentration reflects both the state's early adoption of data center infrastructure and the dominance of the Sabey footprint, which also includes SDC Columbia in East Wenatchee, powered by regional hydroelectric supply. No other operator with facilities in Washington publishes capacity on their spec page.

Sabey Data Centers operates the facility as part of a national footprint of seven campuses totaling nearly 400 MW, making SDC Seattle a secondary asset within a portfolio that includes newer hyperscale builds in Austin and Ashburn. Whether this Tukwila campus matters to AI scaling depends on whether the operator allocates its 54 MW campus-wide capacity to high-density training workloads or to legacy colocation and enterprise tenants; the published specifications do not indicate how the power is split between buildings or what compute density the operator targets.
